title: Automated Quality Control for Precision Manufacturing
business: High-precision electronics manufacturers requiring automated visual inspection of circuit boards.
problem: Traditional convolutional neural networks struggle with long-range dependencies across complex board layouts, leading to high false-rejection rates for subtle defects.
solution: Vision Transformer (ViT) processes the image as a sequence of patches, allowing the self-attention mechanism to model global relationships between distant components on the board, which improves defect detection accuracy.
steps: Divide high-resolution circuit board images into fixed-size square patches.
Flatten patches into a sequence and prepend a learnable classification token.
Apply positional embeddings to preserve spatial information of the patches.
Pass the sequence through multiple transformer encoder layers to compute global attention.
Use the final classification token to output the defect status of the board.
outcome: Improved consistency in defect identification across diverse board designs without requiring manual feature engineering.
limitation: ViT models require large datasets for pre-training to achieve high performance; check for overfitting by monitoring validation loss on smaller, domain-specific datasets.

questions.question: In Automated Quality Control for Precision Manufacturing, why is ViT preferred over traditional CNNs?
options: It eliminates the need for image patching entirely.
It uses self-attention to model global relationships between distant components.
It is specifically designed for low-resolution images only.
It requires no pre-training data to function.
questions.explanation: The solution explains that ViT uses self-attention to model global relationships, which addresses the limitation of CNNs in handling complex layouts.
questions.evidence: Vision Transformer (ViT) processes the image as a sequence of patches, allowing the self-attention mechanism to model global relationships between distant components on the board, which improves defect detection accuracy.

questions.question: In Automated Quality Control for Precision Manufacturing, what is a primary limitation of the implementation?
options: The model cannot process images in patches.
The model is too fast to be accurate.
The model requires large datasets for pre-training and may overfit on small sets.
The model requires manual feature engineering for every new board.
questions.explanation: The limitation section explicitly states the need for large pre-training data and the risk of overfitting on small datasets.
questions.evidence: ViT models require large datasets for pre-training to achieve high performance; check for overfitting by monitoring validation loss on smaller, domain-specific datasets.
